To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the public is not aware of the summary care record or HealthSpace and that most people view the summary care record as a positive development, though there is some confusion about what it contains and who can see it.

1) most participants did not know that the SCR and Healthspace existed and had received little information about them, 2) participants were concerned that their data would not be secure, 3) participants were worried that their data would be accessed by others, 4) participants were concerned about the quality of the data in the SCR, 5) participants did not want their data shared, 6) participants wanted control over who accessed their SCR and what data was included in it, and
most people are not aware of the summary care record or HealthSpace, and those who are aware have a mixed view of the benefits and risks of having a shared electronic record.
In summary, our research is concerned with
people's perceptions of a shared electronic record, and the potential of a personal health organiser.
people's views on the SCR, and the potential for HealthSpace to provide a secure and confidential means of viewing it.
the views of the public about the SCR and its associated HealthSpace.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the public are not clear about the summary care record.
the public are largely unaware of the SCR and Healthspace and are not clear about the benefits and risks of having an SCR.
the public are largely positive towards the SCR but have not been informed of its benefits and drawbacks and therefore have not been able to make an informed choice about its use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

patients are more likely to be interested in accessing and using the SCR if it is presented as a tool to support self management of their health, rather than a tool to help their GP or hospital doctor.
the summary care record should be made more explicit to the public, and people should be given more choice over whether they want to opt in or out of it.
patients' attitudes towards the SCR and Healthspace are positive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
people are more likely to be positive about shared electronic records if they have confidence in the healthcare system and the people working in it.
the NHS should not assume that people are willing to share their personal medical records with other health and social care professionals.
people want to be able to access their own record, and that this is a crucial element of a successful SCR programme.
